metadata.title: Matrix as a Mapping of the Plane
metadata.subject: Mathematics
metadata.objective: Show how a matrix maps basis vectors and a shape in the plane.
metadata.learner: Has seen vectors but not matrix geometry.
misconceptions: Matrix multiplication is just elementwise multiplication
expectedUnderstanding: column 1 is the image of e1 and column 2 is the image of e2
every point of the square maps to the matching point of the parallelogram
det A = a here, so area scales by |a| and b is a shear that keeps area

checkpoints.title: Start from the identity
checkpoints.body: The small square is the reference, with corners (0,0), (1,0), (0,1) and (1,1). The animation shows where each corner goes under the matrix. Press continue to run it.

checkpoints.title: The columns are the basis images
checkpoints.body: Column 1 is (a, 0): the image of e1 = (1,0). Column 2 is (b, 1): the image of e2 = (0,1). The two arrows from the origin are exactly those columns, and they are two sides of the parallelogram.

checkpoints.title: Entries mix coordinates
checkpoints.body: The matrix sends (x, y) to (a x + b y, y). Each output coordinate combines both inputs, which is why entry b moves points whose y is not zero. That is not elementwise multiplication of entries and coordinates.

checkpoints.title: Area and collapse
checkpoints.body: The parallelogram's area is |det A| = |a|: moving a stretches it, moving b shears it sideways and leaves the area unchanged. If a reached 0 the square would flatten onto a line and the map would lose information, so this scene keeps a at least 0.4.

narration.text: The reference unit square is mapped to the parallelogram spanned by the matrix columns.
The arrow tips are the columns: the images of the two basis vectors.
Changing a stretches; changing b shears without changing area.

fallback.text: A unit square at the origin is mapped by the matrix with columns (a, 0) and (b, 1). The image is the parallelogram spanned by those columns: increasing a stretches it horizontally, increasing b slides the top edge sideways, and the area equals |a|. The two arrows show where the basis vectors land.

accessibility.alt: A reference unit square at the origin becoming a parallelogram under a matrix; two arrows show the images of the basis vectors, labelled as column 1 and column 2.
